Hi Sophie / Raj,

Thanks — this is exactly the sort of detail we like to pin down early. High-level answers below; Karthik and Jonas are looped for the deeper technical detail. I'll also attach a one-page cutover timeline we typically use.

- Key exportability: yes — we support customer-managed KEKs that are marked non-exportable inside the HSM. Redwood never has plaintext access to a non-exportable key.
- Protocols: we integrate with AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM; for on-prem we support PKCS#11 and KMIP connectors (we supply a connector daemon when network restrictions require an outbound-only egress proxy).
- TLS / mTLS: our control-plane-to-HSM management supports TLS1.3 and mTLS for admin channels; client certs can be uploaded and rotated.
- Rotation / rewrap: typical approach is staged rewrap with dual-keystore support; planned cutover for active workloads is usually non-disruptive (we can keep reads/writes while rewrapping in background). We recommend a 0–2 hour maintenance window for full verification across services.
- Evidence: we can provide hardware attestation artifacts (certificate chains from the HSM vendor), FIPS validation statements for supported HSM SKUs, and SOC2 evidence mapping.

I've attached our BYOK cutover timeline (byok_cutover_timeline.xlsx) and a short snippet file that documents PKCS#11/KMIP connector config examples (hsm_integration_snippets.txt). How about a technical call tomorrow for the deep-dive? Karthik / Jonas — could you review and add specifics re: rotation mechanics & audit streams?

Sophie / Raj — adding the technical detail you requested. TL;DR: we use an envelope key model keyed by a customer KEK that resides in your HSM (non-exportable). Application flow and migration steps are included.

1) Key hierarchy and flow
  - Customer KEK (KEK_cust) is generated/imported into your HSM (CloudHSM / Dedicated or on-prem). KEK_cust marked non-exportable.
  - Redwood issues ephemeral envelope keys (E_k) per-tenant for encrypting objects. E_k is wrapped (Enc(KEK_cust, E_k)) and stored alongside metadata.
  - At runtime, Redwood requests unwrapping from the HSM via a secure admin channel that requires mTLS and per-call auth; plaintext of E_k is only in memory in an isolated, FIPS-aligned runtime and cleared post-operation.

2) Protocols & connectors
  - Cloud: AWS CloudHSM/Azure Dedicated HSM supported via vendor APIs. We use vendor SDKs and a hardened connector for key operations.
  - On-prem: PKCS#11 or KMIP connectors. We provide a connector daemon that runs in your VPC/on-prem network and proxies KMIP/PKCS#11 calls over TLS to the HSM. The daemon supports pinning to certs and NAT traversal via an egress-only design.

3) No-export guarantee and attestation
  - For supported SKUs (we'll confirm your selected model), vendor attestation reports (signed) prove that private key material cannot be extracted (non-exportable flag enforced by HSM firmware). We include the attestation chain and vendor certificate when requested.

4) Rotation & rewrap approach (detailed)
  - Phase 0 (preparation): create new KEK_cust_v2 in the HSM and publish its public key; Redwood begins dual-wrapping new E_k with both KEK_cust and KEK_cust_v2 (dual-write).
  - Phase 1 (background rewrap): a background rewrap job iterates over stored wrapped envelope keys, asks the HSM to unwrap with KEK_cust and rewrap with KEK_cust_v2, writing a new wrapped entry. Each item is validated via checksum.
  - Phase 2 (cutover): switch read-path to prefer KEK_cust_v2 wrapped entries (instantaneous flag flip); keep KEK_cust active for rollback for configurable retention (we recommend 7 days).
  - Phase 3 (retire): after validation and retention period, schedule a secure erase of KEK_cust subject to compliance approval.
  - Expected application outage: none required for most workloads. For large accounts with multi-tenant storage, we recommend a maintenance window for final verification; rewrap is throttled to keep tail latency within SLOs.

5) TLS / mTLS specifics
  - We require TLS1.3 for admin channels and recommend cipher suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.
  - mTLS is supported; you can upload CA chain and rotate client certs. We support cert rotation with zero-downtime by accepting a small overlap window (old & new certs accepted for a configurable grace period).

6) Auditability & backups
  - All HSM operation requests (unwrap/wrap) are logged with request-id, timestamp, caller identity, and HSM response code and retained per your policy; logs are available for export to your SIEM.
  - Snapshots of wrapped keys are opaque blobs; we recommend maintaining wrapped-key backups in encrypted storage. Restores require the KEK in the HSM to be present to rehydrate.

7) Practical notes for on-prem FIPS HSMs
  - If you require a FIPS-validated on-prem HSM with physical attestation, we will run an initial connectivity & attestation workshop. Provisioning time depends on procurement but technical cutover steps are the same.

If helpful I can provide a short sample script for the PKCS#11 calls and a sample audit export. Attaching a small snippet file now.

Raj / Sophie — thanks for the follow-up. Below is a compact cutover checklist and our answers to your specifics. I've included expected owners and an estimated timeline for each step. Attaching the formal timeline spreadsheet as well.

Cutover checklist (compact) — HelixBio BYOK migration to customer HSM
Pre-cutover (2–4 weeks)
  1) Procurement & HSM provisioning (Infra owner): order HSM SKU with FIPS prefix if required; obtain vendor attestation certificate. (ETA: dependent on procurement, vendor lead times)
  2) Network & connector setup (Infra/Network): deploy Redwood-provided connector daemon in staging network; exchange and pin Redwood control-plane certs. Validate NAT/egress.
  3) Test attestation & API access (Security): run vendor attestation flow; verify signed attestation blob; validate unwrapping workflow in staging.
  4) Policy & retention sign-off (Legal/Security): confirm rollback retention (we recommend 7 days) and escalation path.

Cutover window (recommended 2 hours maintenance window for final validation)
  5) Create KEK_v2 in HSM (Customer Infra) and publish pubkey to Redwood.
  6) Dual-write mode ON (Redwood): new E_k are wrapped with both KEK_v1 and KEK_v2.
  7) Background rewrap job (Redwood): throttle to SLOs; run until >99.9% keys validated.
  8) Flip read preference to KEK_v2 (Redwood flag flip). Validate end-to-end decryption on sample sets.
  9) Monitor & validate (joint): run integrity scans, compare checksums, review HSM audit logs.
 10) Rollback window (customer trigger): if issues, flip back to KEK_v1 and halt new writes.
 11) Retire KEK_v1 (Customer): after retention, schedule key retirement / secure erase.

Answers to Raj's points:
  - Cipher restrictions: yes — we can enforce a restricted cipher list for your admin endpoints; we will add AES-256-only suites per your policy.
  - Client cert rotation: we support automated uploads via API and a webhook model to accept rotated certs. Vault-issued short-lived certs are compatible; Redwood accepts overlapping certs for a grace period to avoid interruption.
  - Large keyset rewrap (~2M objects): plan to run rewrap in batches; expected total wall-clock time depends on object size and HSM unwrap/rewrap throughput. In our experience, with aggressive parallelization and throttling, the background rewrap can complete without customer-visible downtime — but we recommend a short maintenance window to finish final verification. We'll run a capacity estimate once we have sample object sizes and a staging run.
